layer: 1. Product quality and failure intelligence for appliance brands
payer: Brand service/quality head; budget line = warranty provision + customer-service cost. FY26 accruals (FACT): Whirlpool Rs90.85 Cr (1.22% of standalone revenue), Voltas Rs113.72 Cr (0.80%), Blue Star Rs65.76 Cr (0.53%; FY25 0.92%), Havells warranty+e-waste Rs401.55 Cr (1.79%); LG FY25 Rs125.6 Cr (0.52%) on 788,911 warranty claims = about Rs1,590 a claim (DERIVED). Whirlpool customer-service expense Rs128.8 Cr (FACT).
price_model: Annual enterprise licence per brand (data feed + dashboard), optionally priced as a share of warranty savings
price_high: Rs1 Cr a year (ASSUMPTION); global vendors publish no prices (UNKNOWN)
india_market_size_cr: Budget pool Rs475-1,140 Cr a year of warranty cost in AC + fridge + washing machine (DERIVED: Rs95,000 Cr category sales, Redseer via LG RHP x 0.5-1.2%). Software wallet only Rs10-25 Cr a year (DERIVED: ~20 brands x Rs50 L-1.25 Cr, ASSUMPTION)
comparables: PTC (Servigistics/4CS inside PTC; Schneider agreed to buy PTC at $22.6B in 2026, FACT); Syncron (owners, revenue UNKNOWN); Bruviti (claims >15% cost cut on repair-vs-replace, 20% fewer repeat failures; customers Electrolux, Samsung; pricing UNKNOWN); Tavant, After Inc, SAS Field Quality: revenue/price UNKNOWN (pages blocked)
time_to_first_cr: Year 4-6 (ASSUMPTION: needs 1-2 lakh records per category and 2-3 brand contracts at Rs30-50 L)
entry_feasibility: LOW-MEDIUM. Brands already hold in-warranty claims (LG handled 9M+ service claims in FY25 through its own Engineer App with GPS and closure codes). Keepwell's unique slice is out-of-warranty failures, install quality and Tier 2/3 field conditions, but its sample is small and regional until ~30+ clusters. Enterprise sales cycle is long.

layer: 2. Installation and claims verification (brands, extended-warranty providers, retailers)
payer: Brands (proof an authorised install/repair happened correctly before paying an install or warranty claim); extended-warranty and protection providers (OneAssist, Onsitego, Zopper, Servify) verifying unit, serial and condition at enrolment and at claim; retailers (dispute evidence). Budget line: warranty cost and claims operations.
price_model: Per verified record (photo + serial + geo-time + checklist) bundled into jobs Keepwell already does; SaaS seat or API fee for third-party technicians
price_base: Rs40 per record (ASSUMPTION; about 2.5% of LG's ~Rs1,590 cost per warranty claim, DERIVED)
price_high: Rs100 per record (ASSUMPTION); Tractable and ClaimGenius per-claim prices UNKNOWN
gross_margin: 80-90% when bundled into an existing visit (ASSUMPTION); 20-30% if a separate visit is needed (Step 0 job economics)
india_market_size_cr: Rs85-220 Cr a year (DERIVED: ~35M large-appliance installs a year (prior research) x Rs20-50 + ~4.3M warranty claims (DERIVED: LG's 32 claims per Rs1 Cr revenue x Rs1.33 lakh Cr home-appliance market) x Rs30-100). Fraud/leakage share in Indian warranty claims UNKNOWN
comparables: Tractable (photo AI for insurance claims; $1B valuation 2021, $65M from SoftBank Vision Fund 2 in 2023, FACT; revenue UNKNOWN); Servify (Rs5,660 Cr valuation Mar 2025, ~Rs781 Cr revenue FY25, loss-making); OneAssist (Rs623 Cr, 4.1% EBITDA FY25); Onsitego (~Rs278 Cr FY25); ClaimGenius (UNKNOWN)
time_to_first_cr: Year 3-4 (DERIVED: Rs1 Cr = 2.5 L records at Rs40, about 18 cluster-years at ~13.5k jobs a cluster; or 1-2 enterprise API deals)
entry_feasibility: HIGH. Every Keepwell job already captures model, serial, install date, photos and parts. Marginal cost per record is near zero. It also supports the brand-authorisation pitch (the biggest lever in Step 0). Main limits: brands verify their own ASC network already (LG 'Happiness code' + GPS), so the buyer is the gap between brand, dealer-installer and protection provider.
